subject: fire salamander
title: Fire Salamanders Have Glowed All Along. We Just Couldn't See It

scenes.text: This salamander has been glowing all along. Nobody noticed.
The fire salamander is black and yellow, and its skin oozes poison.
Shine ultraviolet light on it, and its yellow belly and sides glow blue-green.
Even the goo from its skin glands keeps glowing for more than a day after it's released.
Our eyes can't see ultraviolet, so the glow stayed invisible to everyone studying it.
Moonlight carries more UV than daylight. At night, it may be shining for eyes that aren't ours.

description:
Fire salamanders glow blue-green under ultraviolet light, a 2026 study found.
The glow comes mainly from the yellow belly and sides and from skin-gland secretions, which stay fluorescent for more than 24 hours after release.
What other animals do you think are glowing where we can't see it?
thumbnail_text: IT GLOWS. YOU CAN'T SEE IT
first_comment: Nobody yet knows which chemical makes the glow; the researchers are still trying to identify it. Would you go looking for one with a UV torch?
